periodic-timer-loop.title: Run periodic work with PeriodicTimer
periodic-timer-loop.short: Repeat asynchronous work at a regular interval.
periodic-timer-loop.summary: PeriodicTimer lets code await each tick, so periodic work does not need to block a thread with Thread.Sleep.
periodic-timer-loop.why: The wait does not occupy a thread and cancellation can be expressed with a CancellationToken.
periodic-timer-loop.tips: Dispose the timer, commonly with using, and consider what should happen when one iteration takes longer than the period.

linked-cancellation-token.title: Combine multiple CancellationTokens
linked-cancellation-token.short: Merge several cancellation conditions into one token.
linked-cancellation-token.summary: CreateLinkedTokenSource combines conditions such as request cancellation and application shutdown into one CancellationToken for downstream operations.
linked-cancellation-token.why: Any linked source can stop the operation while downstream APIs only need one token.
linked-cancellation-token.tips: Dispose the linked CancellationTokenSource with using.

valuetask-single-consumption.title: Do not casually await a ValueTask more than once
valuetask-single-consumption.short: Treat a ValueTask as a single-consumption value unless its contract says otherwise.
valuetask-single-consumption.summary: Unlike Task, a ValueTask is not guaranteed to support being stored and awaited repeatedly. Implementations backed by IValueTaskSource may reject multiple consumption.
valuetask-single-consumption.why: ValueTask can use specialized backing implementations to avoid allocations rather than always wrapping a reusable Task.
valuetask-single-consumption.tips: If several places need the result, await once and store the resulting value. Check the contract before using AsTask as an alternative.

interlocked-counter.title: Update shared counters with Interlocked
interlocked-counter.short: Perform simple shared numeric updates atomically.
interlocked-counter.summary: Interlocked.Increment and related operations update simple shared values atomically without taking a lock.
interlocked-counter.why: An expression such as x++ consists of read, modify, and write steps, so racing threads can otherwise lose updates.
interlocked-counter.tips: Use a lock or another synchronization mechanism when several values must change together under one invariant.

collections-marshal-span.title: Access List<T> storage with CollectionsMarshal.AsSpan
collections-marshal-span.short: Use a List<T> as a Span<T> for specialized performance-sensitive code.
collections-marshal-span.summary: CollectionsMarshal.AsSpan exposes the element storage of a List<T> directly, which can avoid copies and some access overhead.
collections-marshal-span.why: The speed comes with stricter rules: changing the list size while the span is in use can invalidate assumptions about its backing storage.
collections-marshal-span.tips: Use it only where measurement justifies the complexity, and do not structurally modify the List while the span is alive.

searchvalues-repeated-search.title: Reuse repeated searches with SearchValues<T>
searchvalues-repeated-search.short: Prepare a set of values once for repeated searches.
searchvalues-repeated-search.summary: SearchValues<T> represents a prepared set used by Span search operations such as IndexOfAny and can be reused across many searches.
searchvalues-repeated-search.why: For repeated searches against the same set, the runtime can use an efficient representation and search strategy.
searchvalues-repeated-search.tips: For a single tiny search, a simpler IndexOfAny overload may still be clearer.

composite-format-reuse.title: Reuse parsed formatting with CompositeFormat
composite-format-reuse.short: Parse a repeated composite format once and reuse it.
composite-format-reuse.summary: CompositeFormat.Parse creates a parsed representation that can be reused by string.Format when the same composite format is applied repeatedly.
composite-format-reuse.why: Hot paths that repeatedly use one fixed format can avoid reparsing the format string each time.
composite-format-reuse.tips: Keep ordinary interpolation where it is clearer; consider CompositeFormat for genuinely repeated formatting work.

guid-create-version7.title: Create time-ordered IDs with Guid.CreateVersion7
guid-create-version7.short: Generate version 7 UUIDs instead of random version 4 UUIDs.
guid-create-version7.summary: Guid.CreateVersion7 creates a version 7 UUID containing a timestamp component. Its ordering characteristics can improve locality for some indexed storage workloads.
guid-create-version7.why: Completely random identifiers can scatter inserts across an index, while version 7 values have time-related ordering.
guid-create-version7.tips: Do not treat the timestamp as secret or the value as a strict sequence, and verify how the target database orders UUID values.

task-wheneach-completion-order.title: Process tasks in completion order with Task.WhenEach
task-wheneach-completion-order.short: Consume results as individual tasks finish.
task-wheneach-completion-order.summary: Task.WhenEach enumerates a set of tasks in completion order, allowing fast results to be processed without waiting for the slowest task first.
task-wheneach-completion-order.why: Task.WhenAll is ideal when all work must finish before continuing, but completion-order processing is useful for streaming intermediate results.
task-wheneach-completion-order.tips: The sequence yields completed Task objects; await each yielded task to observe its result or exception.

cancellation-token-register-dispose.title: Dispose CancellationToken.Register registrations
cancellation-token-register-dispose.short: Remove cancellation callbacks when they are no longer needed.
cancellation-token-register-dispose.summary: CancellationToken.Register returns a CancellationTokenRegistration. Disposing it when the callback is no longer needed prevents a long-lived token from retaining unnecessary callbacks and references.
cancellation-token-register-dispose.why: A registration can keep objects captured by its callback reachable for as long as the registration remains attached.
cancellation-token-register-dispose.tips: When the registration lifetime matches a scope, express it directly with using.
